reviews.title: Bait and bill
reviews.text: The underlying functionality is meh. Setting up a workout for the first time is a bit confusing and not super intuitive. But more than that the big problem I have is that it simply wouldn’t work past the first week (or about 3-4 workouts for me) without a subscription. This app wasn’t advertised as a “free trial”, but that’s what it is. I don’t have a problem with devs getting paid for their work, but an app that’s advertised as “free” should actually work for more than a couple days before a subscription is required. A basic interval timer shouldn’t require a recurring monthly invoice IMO. Will be deleting the app today.

reviews.title: App works well but demo far too short
reviews.text: From the brief use I got from the app it seemed to work well. However it limits the number of times you use the app to 2 workouts (and I unknowingly wasted one while messing with the settings) before requiring a fee. While the optional one time fee alongside a subscription option isn’t a bad idea, got far too little use out of the app before getting locked out to ever consider splashing anywhere near their asking prices. Give us a chance to use it first before reaching for our wallet. Who knows, the one time I used the app it seemed to work well so may very well come back, but there are countless other timer app options to test first before that scenario.

reviews.title: Don’t Waste Your Time!
reviews.text:
Go download Simple Interval Timer by Su Au Huang. 

It has everything you need for a workout timer without the BS.

I first tried this POS and did a test set to see if the app worked as intended. Lo and behold, you only get one free workout before you have to pay. I skipped through the sets to test the round count by the way and it still counted that as my one free workout. Do yourself a favor and delete this or better yet never download it and go get something that does the exact same thing for free elsewhere. 0/5 stars. 

Devs if you see this, don’t bother trying to fix anything or reach out. You’re obviously making money. I hope you fail though, it’s nothing personal. I just believe you’re taking advantage of people who could be getting a decent product for free and then choosing to give when they can.

reviews.title: Too touchy
reviews.text: Great idea, but could be designed better. I need a way to time one minute of running (“Work”) followed by three minutes of walking (“Rest”), X10. Problem I am having is it’s too easy to accidentally make something unpredictable occur like skipping to the next section or stopping the timer altogether. Ideally if I could turn off the screen and allow the app to run in the background, that would be perfect. This would eliminate stray screen touches, and unpredictable results.  Unfortunately turning off the screen stops the app. If you’re wanting to use this app for this same purpose, you might want to pass on it. I wish I knew of a way to fix this or if there was an alternate app I could use.

reviews.title: Hilarious cash grab
reviews.text:
I just need to write a review because I’ve never seen anything quite like this app. I was expecting to get either a version with some reduced functionality that I could pay to upgrade or a free trial of the paid version that I would eventually need to pay to keep using.

What I did not expect is that I put one workout into the app, let the timer run to test it out and make sure I had set it up right, and then the app never let me run the timer again to actually work out. It just comes up with the popup imploring me to either pay a monthly subscription for a timer or use a 7 day free trial to decide whether I want to pay a monthly subscription for a timer.

I thought I was losing my mind until seeing other reviews saying the same thing. Genuinely comical in its audacity.

reviews.title: Needs Documentation
reviews.text: I downloaded this to help me manage my physical therapy regimen.   I had been using a stopwatch app and was struggling to manage both the interval and rep count.   This looked like it would be just the ticket, but I can’t find any directions at all.  I tried the support page, but no keyword I entered got me any information.  I was able to enter names for my different exercises, but they all have different hold times and rep counts and I can’t figure out how to assign those to individual exercises.   It’s probably easy, but with no help menu or user guide, I can’t make it work.
